publicationMetadataPlan.creator: OpenAI built-in image generation
publicationMetadataPlan.mediaDescription: Review-only scientific algorithmic anatomical or pathology reconstruction, not a photograph, scan, histology slide, patient record, or diagnostic image
publicationMetadataPlan.sourceUse: NLM MeSH supplies controlled condition identity and scope; official NIH or CDC sources supply conservative anatomical and communication boundaries only. No source image or design is copied.

reviewStandard: Current controlled condition identity, conservative non-diagnostic anatomy or systems orientation, non-stigmatizing communication, complete pale edge field, crop-safe geometry, and exact prompt frozen before exactly one generation call per cleared route. Observed output controls later metadata.

assets.scientificFinding: Current inherited progressive neurodegenerative condition with variable movement, cognitive, and behavioral manifestations. A neutral neuroanatomical orientation plate cannot establish diagnosis, pathology, or stage.
Current systemic arterial-pressure condition established by measurement rather than appearance. Neutral heart and artery models must not imply visible diagnosis or universal damage.
Current umbrella for chronic structural inflammatory bowel disorders including Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis. Selected wall patterns are illustrative, non-universal, and non-diagnostic.
Current disorder of gut-brain interaction in which symptoms occur without visible digestive-tract damage. The plate must remain structurally intact and visually distinct from IBD.

Current heterogeneous post-acute condition with many possible symptoms and body systems. A selected multisystem plate must not reduce it to one lesion, biomarker, mechanism, stage, or universal symptom set.

Current heterogeneous mental disorder affecting feeling, thinking, and daily activities with multiple contributing domains. Representation must be non-stigmatizing and must not assert a visible lesion, neurotransmitter, mechanism, patient stereotype, or diagnostic sign.
